NBA Shot Selection Analytics

How many more points could an NBA player score by shifting shots toward their strongest areas?

Compare two players’ shot mixes
Page sections
ExplorerHow the model worksLimitationsDefinitionsSources and code

How the model works

We analyze 1,507 player-seasons from 2021–22 through 2025–26, fitting each season separately. Players need 250 included attempts across 20 games. We exclude shots outside the half-court boundary.

Method

Data and seasons

Estimating shooting chances

We divide the court into 156 cells, about four feet across, and estimate make probabilities from each player’s made and missed shots.

A Bayesian conditional autoregressive model connects cells that share an edge. Evidence from neighboring cells helps estimate shooting chances where attempts are sparse.

Players have separate shooting maps but share the smoothing strength. We retain uncertainty around each estimate. Empty cells can have estimated make probabilities, but cannot receive relocated shots.

Finding areas that can receive shots

A receiving cell needs at least 10 attempts and a 90% model probability of beating the player’s historical points per attempt. We calculate shot value from the player’s observed mix of twos and threes in that cell.

One qualifying cell can support relocation. Each receiving cell can hold at most 50% of attempts after additions. A cell already above 50% keeps its historical shots but receives none. Without eligible capacity, scores and gains remain unavailable.

Choosing which shots move

We move attempts from below-baseline cells, weakest first. Individual makes and misses inform ability estimates but do not determine which shots move.

The slider requests 0–25% in five-point steps. Movement stops at the request, available weak-source shots, or receiving capacity. A faded marker represents a fractional attempt at the boundary.

We distribute moved shots in proportion to historical usage in receiving cells. When one fills, we redistribute the remainder among supported cells with room. Higher slider settings retain earlier selections; at least 75% of volume stays in its historical locations.

Estimating points and uncertainty

We freeze the relocation plan, then compare historical and changed mixes across 4,000 joint ability draws. Each comparison uses the same make probabilities for both mixes.

Gains show the mean difference across draws. Scores show the median after restricting each draw’s score to 0–100. Ranges span the fifth through ninety-fifth percentiles.

Formulas

The equations apply to one joint ability draw. Historical and relocated mixes share the same make probabilities.

Variable key

c, s
A court cell and the requested slider share (0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, or 25%).
A
Total included shot attempts in the selected season.
pc
Modeled make probability in cell c for one joint simulation.
vc
Cell point value: 2 plus the observed share of three-point attempts in that player-season cell.
wc, w′c(s)
Historical and relocated shares of all included shots in cell c; the prime (′) marks the changed distribution at request s.
Ec, EPPS
Expected points per shot in a cell, and the abbreviation for expected points per shot.
current, relocated
Subscript labels for the historical and feasible changed shot mixes.
Season gain, Gain per 100
Extra points over A season attempts or over 100 attempts at request s.
Score
One simulation’s comparison of current and feasible 25% expected points per shot, before the 0–100 limit.
Σc
Add across court cells; a subscript c identifies the cell.
Q0.05, Q0.95
The fifth and ninety-fifth percentiles of the 4,000 calculated gains or limited scores.
Range90%
The interval between those percentiles: the middle 90% of calculated values.
=, ×, −
Equals, multiply and subtract. A fraction bar means divide.
( ), [ ], %
Parentheses and brackets group terms; s is the requested share. Range brackets enclose endpoints.

Equations

1. Expected points in a cell

Ec = pc × vc

Multiply the chance of a make by the cell’s two-point and three-point value.

2. Current expected points per shot

EPPScurrent = Σc (wc × pc × vc)

Weight each cell’s expected points by how often the player shot there.

3. Expected points after relocation

EPPSrelocated(s) = Σc (w′c(s) × pc × vc)

Use the changed shot shares while keeping the same estimated shooting ability.

4. Extra points in the selected season

Season gain(s) = A × [EPPSrelocated(s) − EPPScurrent]

Apply the difference per shot to the player’s included season attempts.

5. Extra points per 100 shots

Gain per 100(s) = 100 × [EPPSrelocated(s) − EPPScurrent]

Express the same difference over 100 attempts, regardless of season shot volume.

6. Shot Selection Score

Score = 100 × EPPScurrentEPPSrelocated(25%)

Compare the past mix with the feasible mix at the largest slider request.

The calculation limits each of the 4,000 scores to 0–100, then displays their median. Dividing two displayed averages does not reproduce that median of ratios. The 25% request uses the actual feasible movement when source shots, evidence, or the 50% destination cap prevent moving all 25%.

7. Estimated Range (90%)

Range90% = [Q0.05, Q0.95]

Keep the middle 90% of the model’s 4,000 calculated values.

Gains display the average across those values. Scores display the median after the 0–100 limit. The ranges reflect uncertainty in modeled ability, not a simulation of future makes and misses.

Where the values come from

  • Make probability (pc): The player’s season-specific spatial shooting model supplies 4,000 joint estimates across court cells.
  • Point value (vc): For each player and season, divide three-point attempts in a cell by all attempts in that cell, then add 2. A cell with only twos has value 2; one with only threes has value 3. A cell crossing the arc uses the player’s observed mix, not its center’s location. Empty cells have no observed point value and receive no shot share; the calculation sets their zero-weight contribution to the sums to zero.
  • Current shares (wc): Divide attempts in each cell by the player’s total included season attempts.
  • Relocated shares (w′c(s)): Remove shots weakest first from below-baseline areas. Add them to supported areas in proportion to existing usage, redistributing when an area reaches the 50% cap. Freeze this plan before evaluating the 4,000 estimates.
  • Feasible movement: Use the smallest of the requested share, eligible weak-source share, and supported receiving capacity. Each supported cell’s added capacity is 50% minus its historical share, or zero if that share is already 50% or more; add those capacities across supported cells.
  • Uncertainty: Apply the fixed shot shares and point values to each joint model estimate, then summarize the resulting gains and scores with the ranges above.

Unavailable relocation keeps scores and gains missing, including at 0%. None of these equations turns missing evidence into a zero estimate.

Validation and research

How the model was tested

We split 2025–26 games into fitting, court-size selection and final-test groups, keeping each game’s shots together. On 39,212 shots from 246 unseen games, the selected model beat a smooth-curve alternative on the predeclared prediction test. Calibration showed no clear disadvantage; uncertainty showed no clear advantage for low-volume players.

After testing, we refit on all included shots. The other four seasons use separate fits with the same specification, without repeating model selection. Checks cover missing results, shot counts, reproducible movement, uncertainty ranges and the receiving cap.

Limitations

  • Relocation is a hypothetical change in shot mix. These estimates cannot establish that moving shots would cause scoring gains.
  • Players’ roles, teammates, coaches and available opportunities constrain shot locations.
  • We omit defense, contests, opponent quality and defensive reactions to repeated shot patterns.
  • We omit game situation, pressure and playoff context.
  • We omit shot creation, pass quality, technique and part of free-throw value.
  • We omit fatigue, injuries, travel and changing health.
  • We hold ability fixed as volume moves, though success may decline at higher volume.
  • Four-foot cells, the 25% request limit and the 50% receiving cap are modeling choices.
  • The 90% range covers uncertainty within the model.
  • The score compares a player with their own mix. It cannot rank overall talent.
  • One-area estimates warrant caution. Cyan diamonds represent hypothetical attempts.
  • Separate season fits cannot forecast development, aging or team changes.
  • Eligibility, court boundaries, evidence requirements and capacity can prevent estimates.
  • Do not use these scenarios for coaching recommendations or betting.

Definitions

Shot relocation

Move attempts from weaker estimated scoring areas to supported stronger areas while preserving total volume. Individual shot outcomes do not decide movement.

Shots to Move

The maximum requested share. A 25% request can move fewer attempts when source shots or capacity run out. Fractional attempts reflect volume shares.

Extra Points in the Selected Season

Estimated points gained over the included season attempts. LeBron’s 2025–26 example at 25% adds 157 modeled points across 919 shots. His official total stays unchanged.

Extra Points per 100 Shots

The same gain per 100 attempts: +17.0 in LeBron’s example. Negative values mean fewer expected points.

Shot Selection Score

Historical efficiency as a percentage of feasible efficiency at the 25% request, bounded to 0–100. A score of 90 means about 90% of that scenario’s points per shot. We report the median across model draws.

Estimated Range (90%)

The middle 90% of model estimates. LeBron’s example spans 129–183 points. This range excludes uncertainty outside the model.

Estimate from One Area

One cell passes the evidence rules and receives shots until source volume or its 50% cap runs out.

Make-chance map

Estimated make probabilities by cell, using neighboring evidence where shots are sparse. Relocation requires separate shot-value and evidence checks.

Area with Evidence for Moving Shots

A diamond marks a cell with 10 or more attempts and at least 90% probability of beating the player’s current points per attempt. Capacity determines whether it can receive shots.

No Clear Area for Moving Shots

No cell passes both evidence rules. Historical shots and the make-chance map remain available. Missing evidence does not establish ideal shot selection.

No Room to Move More Shots

Qualifying cells have no capacity under the 50% cap. Scores and gains remain unavailable.

Estimated Points per Shot

Estimated make probability multiplied by the cell’s observed two-point and three-point value.

Sources and code

Project details

  • Data: Recorded NBA field-goal attempts in five separate regular seasons.
  • Approach: Estimate shooting chances by location, then test a limited change in shot mix.
  • Seasons: 2021–22 through 2025–26.
  • Analysis code: View the analysis on GitHub.
